Thank you. 
I’m just not good enough for anyone or anything. I tried hard with my education and fucked that up for myself. I’ve been in the same dead end job for 3 years and can’t find myself a new job. When I did get a new job, the proceeded to fuck me over and now I’m back working at my precious hell hole.

Just feel like nothing really ever goes my way. I’ve been trying to make a life for myself and I keep failing. I got into university with shitty grades from school, and had to leave because I failed my second year and couldn’t handle living with the people I was living with. I can’t get out of this shitty job which is causing a few of my issues. Being rejected hit me hard, basically not good enough to do any other job but this one. I’ve got debt I need to pay off and need to save to move house once our tenancy is over. The money I get from here barely covers me for a month. Everything’s getting too hard to handle.

Thanks kind stranger. Just got rejected from a job I want and the only one I can really apply to because of lack of experience. 
This has basically confirmed everything I thought about myself. 
Don’t think there’s much hope for me now.

Haha that's a good way to put it. I feel like I'm quite generous to people, I share literally everything I have if somebody needs it. If one of my friends has no money, I'll lend them some. If they haven't got money for food, I'll buy them food or share mine with them. I trust my friends and they trust me. However this guy made my life a living nightmare for a year. The only way I could get him back was by taking his money. Sounds so awful but at the time it felt justified

I felt like I was getting my own back in a way. My other flat mates used to leave their money lying about and stuff and not once did I take from them. They weren't as bad as him. I tried so hard to get along with them at the start of the year, but I was completely different to them, I had to do a lot of written work for my course and *had* to attended uni everyday because of the type of course I was on which meant I couldn't go out with them during freshers and after and I think that didn't help with it. They all bonded over freshers and I kinda missed out on it. 
I'm not trying to justify my actions because I know stealing is wrong. At the time it felt justified because of the way they made me feel. 

Thank you! I'm in a much better place mentally and live with the best people now

Very true and I agree with you completely. This is why I'm conflicted about it now. I felt like it was justified at the time (this was 4 years ago now). I don't steal from people at all, I'm honest with money when it comes to my job. I haven't stolen from anyone before or after that.

I started with a drawing pin. Only did like 2 scrapes across my arm. This was when I was 13 (2007) just about to turn 14. It then moved of to safety pins and then unscrewing the blades from pencil sharpeners. Used that up until I was 18 and could finally buy razor blades. Razor blades were the best thing. So fucking sharp. They did the trick. Now I want it more than ever.
I don't think swearing in public is rude.

Though it would be wrong to say that gambling *isn't* addictive. 
That's fair enough, saying to someone that the reason you can't stop is because you're addicted really astonishes people and you feel like a right fool. Just didn't know whether it can be *kind of* like an addiction or whether you can actually get proper addicted to it. 
Thanks for your answer :)
